title: Williamsburg Bridge — source-governed digital twin
summary: A browser 3D model of the Williamsburg Bridge in which every part carries its provenance, so a reader can ask of any surface how it is known and get a real answer, including 'we do not'.

narrative.problem: The national record for the Williamsburg Bridge, HAER NY-128, contains no measured drawings and one sentence of dimensions, so any 3D model of it either guesses or has to say where its evidence runs out.
narrative.decision: No dimension may exist in the model without a registered source and an explicit confidence grade; geometry provenance is derived in the build, and the published site deploys only if the traceability and regression test suites pass.
narrative.tradeoff: Almost everything is inferred, so turning off INFERRED in the viewer makes the bridge disappear, and unknowns such as the side-span length stay deliberately round placeholders instead of plausible guesses.
narrative.limitation: Milestone 1 only: no part is measured, 32 of 57 parts are graded D, 11 questions are open with 14 registered source conflicts, and the sourced approaches end about 22 m above mean high water because the sources do not close.
narrative.caveat: A schematic, not a survey: inferred parts render dashed, dimensions are withheld where provenance is not documented, and the HAER photographs are reference imagery only.
